books.section: Topic 6.11 Reform in the Gilded Age
The Silver Issue and the Populist Movement

stimulus.text:
“I was once a tool of oppression,
And as green as a sucker could be,
And monopolies banded together
To beat a poor hayseed like me.
The railroads and old party bosses
Together did sweetly agree;
And they thought there would be little trouble
In working a hayseed like me.
But now I’ve roused up a little
And their greed and corruption I see,
And the ticket we vote next November
Will be made of hayseeds like me.”

(“The Hayseed,” Farmers’ Alliance song, sung in Kansas in 1890)
stimulus.source_note: “The Hayseed,” Farmers’ Alliance song of the 1890s, sung to the tune of “Save a Poor Sinner Like Me.” Public domain; wording checked against the Nebraska Folklore Pamphlet 18 transcript (Federal Writers’ Project, 1938) of the Farmers’ Alliance paper version.

stem: According to the song, what had the railroads and the party bosses done to the farmer?

options.text: Joined together to beat and exploit him
Helped him sell his crops at fair prices
options.misconception: The song says the bosses agreed to work the farmer, not to help him sell.

options.text: Taught him how to vote in national elections
options.misconception: The song says the farmer roused himself; no one taught him to vote.

options.text: Protected his land from the monopolies
options.misconception: The monopolies and the bosses are on the same side against the farmer.

rationales.A: The song says the railroads and old party bosses together agreed in working a hayseed like him.
rationales.B: Fair prices never appear. The song is a complaint about being beaten, not helped.
rationales.C: The farmer decides his own ticket. No one teaches him to vote.
rationales.D: The bosses stand with the monopolies, not between them and the farmer.
rationales.general:
Take the charge straight from the song.
1. Find the lines about the railroads and old party bosses.
2. They together did sweetly agree.
3. They agreed in working a hayseed like the singer, squeezing the farmer between them.
4. Joining together to work the farmer is the wrong the song names.
Remember: a song’s complaint is the grievance its singers carried into the voting booth.
